missed: ⛔⛔ #1 — THE CHANGE REDS `e2e:gating` ON EVERY COMMIT, AND THE REPO DOCUMENTS THIS EXACT FAILURE HAPPENING BEFORE. `e2e/fog.spec.ts` roll-calls `fogHiddenLayer.children` with an exact 19-entry `expect(r.fogHiddenChildNames).toEqual([...])` — index 0 is `sparkRenderer.container`, index 18 `stinkTowerRenderer.spriteLayer`. The report's prescription ('a new line IMMEDIATELY BEFORE `const sparkRenderer = new SparkRenderer(app, fogHiddenLayer);`') inserts a child at index 0 and shifts all 19. The spec's own comment at index 15 states the consequence verbatim: *"A renderer that takes `fogHiddenLayer` as its parent and does NOT appear here reds `e2e:gating` on every commit afterwards, invisibly to tsc, the 4,780 unit tests and `check:atlas`."* Its index-14 comment records S175 shipping FOUR red commits this way, *"including the one its handoff called green"*. AND `e2e/tower-art.spec.ts:152` reads `above.children[6]` (towerRenderer.layer) and `:295` reads `children[11]` — the fog.spec comments at indices 14 and 15 both note those two probes survived because past inserts were ABOVE them; an insert at index 0 is BELOW both, so both move. `@visual` is `'GATING'` (`ci.e2eLanes.test.ts:66`) and `e2e:gating` is `--grep-invert "@quarantine-flaky|@soak|@perf-measure|@archived-hazard|@races"` (`package.json:18`), so fog.spec (untagged) and tower-art.spec (@visual) both run there — and `e2e.yml` runs it on pull_request. NEITHER FILE IS IN `file_set`. This is the whole S182 lesson in one omission: typecheck green, 4569 unit tests green, build green, CI red forever.

⛔⛔ #2 — THE SIX-DECAL PALETTE IS THE INVISIBILITY BUG THIS REPO ALREADY MEASURED AND FIXED ONCE. `main.ts:287` sets `backgroundColor: 0x000000` and `creatureLift.ts:67-70` records the measurement: *"P2's first cut drew `0x000000` at alpha 0.22 and a pixel sample of the running game showed the board background is **pure black (0,0,0)** — black over black composites to black, so the feature was provably invisible."* The fix was to abandon the dark mark for a SEAT TINT at 0.3. The backdrop the decal sits on is measured 'mean max-channel 22–41 out of 255' (`zoneBackgroundRenderer.ts:18-19`) at 0.55 alpha over that black, i.e. effective ground of roughly RGB (12..23) — and every design-spec prompt ends '**the centre … is open, empty and featureless**', so the tower's own ground is the darkest part of the frame. Now take the report's own numbers: zombie body `0x2a3d18` @ 0.28 over ~(12,18,12) lands at ~(20,30,15) — a delta of ~8/255. Vampires `0x3a0e18` @ 0.34, mummies `0x6b5a44` @ 0.22, orcs `0x3a2a1e` @ 0.20, nagas `0x12303a` @ 0.24 and the demon fissure `0x1a1216` @ 0.5 are all the same class. The report cites the 22–41/255 measurement and draws the OPPOSITE conclusion from it ('a decal brighter than that will read as a sticker … keep decal fills at alpha ≤ ~0.35'). ⭐ AND `drawRotAura` is the proof against it: the only reason that visual reads is its 14 BRIGHT `ROT_TINT` 0x7bbf3a bubbles at alpha 0.18–0.60 — the dark scorch disc underneath is the invisible half. Of the report's six, only zombies and demons carry a comparable bright element; vampires (one 0.40 arc), orcs (two 0.25 dots) and mummies (eight 0.18 grains) do not. So the honest split is NOT 'four for free, one borderline, one wants art' — as specified it is closer to 'two read, three vanish, one wants art', and the correction is free: lead with the race ACCENT hue as the body, keep the dark material as the rim.

⛔ #3 — `blueprintExtent('voltkin')` IS DEGENERATE AND OPTION B PUBLISHES FROM THE VOLTKIN. The report quotes `blueprints.ts:462` — *"`(VOLTKIN_HALF * 2 - 1) * CHAIN_STEP` = **280 px wide and 0 px tall**"* — and then, two sections later, prescribes `markTowerGround(cx, cy, halfW, halfH, …)` at all three publish sites including `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576`, sized from `blueprintExtent`. For the Voltkin that box is 304 × 24 px: a long thin letterbox strip of race material under a TV. Worse, the Voltkin is a godly, not a race building — there is no defensible race ground for it. The branch needs either a per-recipe opt-in flag or an explicit exclusion, and neither is costed.

⛔ #4 — `raceId` IS NOT IN SCOPE AT ANY OF THE THREE PUBLISH SITES. I read all three. `towerRenderer.ts:313` has `sp` (the CreatureSpawner) and `cx, cy`; `structureRampRenderer.ts:223` has `members, bonds, cx, cy, newestTick`; `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576` has `chain, bonds, newestTick, cx, cy`. None has a race. Option B's signature needs `world.players.get(owner)?.raceId` plumbed at three sites plus a fallback for an absent owner — the same resolution order `ownerTint` (`creatureLift.ts:97-104`) already implements and which the branch should reuse rather than reinvent. Small, but it is a third file-touch the report calls 'one line'.

⛔ #5 — A TEST IN A FILE THE REPORT DID LIST WILL GO RED FOR A REASON IT DID NOT NAME. `towerCover.test.ts:298-301` asserts `[...src.matchAll(/of world\.(\w+)\.values\(\)/g)]` over `structureRampRenderer.ts` equals exactly `['creatureSpawners','defenders']`. The report flags the two hand-written filename censuses and misses this one, which is the only mechanically-enumerating test in the file.

⭐ #6 — A FREE, ALREADY-GENERATED, PER-RACE 'TOWER MEETS GROUND' ASSET IS SITTING UNUSED ON DISK, AND THE REPORT NEVER MENTIONS IT. `render/towerFrames.ts:105-110`: `T3_TOWER_STATE_ROWS` maps intact:0, damaged:2, destroyed:3 and the comment says *"row 1 is `spawning` on the tier-3 sheets — deliberately skipped"*. `hostTick.ts:1067-1069` corroborates: *"the shipped tier-3 sprite sheets carry a `spawning` row that no code could draw … The art pipeline authored a spawn animation for a tower the sim never let spawn."* All six sheets ship it — `public/art/race-tier3-towers/t3tower-<race>-atlas.png` + `-anim.json`, which I opened: `"spawning": { "row": 1, "frames": 1, "ticksPerFrame": 1 }`. ⚠ AND THE HONEST MEASUREMENT, WHICH CORRECTS A DOC: `ART_PIPELINE.md` claims *"the owner's 'pulsate, then it rises out of the ground' cinematic is already half-paid-for"* — the shipped manifests say ONE frame per state, not twelve. So it is six unused per-race STILLS of the tower in its emerging state, not an animation. Still zero money, still exactly the 'tower integrated into the ground' register he asked for, and worth putting in front of him alongside the procedural option.

⭐ #7 — TEXTURE DERIVATION FROM AN ALREADY-LOADED ASSET IS A SHIPPED TECHNIQUE HERE, WHICH OPENS A SECOND ZERO-COST PATH. `zoneBackgroundRenderer.ts:237` `function punchPortal(tex: Texture, zone: number, layout: ZoneLayout): Texture` bakes a derived texture through a 2D canvas, once, and caches it (`this.baked`, :425-429). The same mechanism can cut a sub-rect out of the race's ALREADY-DECODED backdrop and draw it, darkened, in the footprint box: zero new fetches, zero new bytes, and the decal is literally made of that race's own ground so it blends by construction — the one thing a Graphics primitive cannot promise. ⚠ Caveat, from the prompts themselves: the CENTRE of every backdrop is 'open, empty and featureless', so the crop must come from the lower edge where the material is. Worth one paragraph in front of the owner because it is free and it is the only option that matches the painted register he cares about.

⚠ #8 — `ci.e2eLanes.test.ts` ENUMERATES SPEC FILES DYNAMICALLY (`readdirSync` at :98 and :149), so a correctly `@races`-tagged new spec needs NO edit to that file. The report lists it conditionally, which is harmless, but it also means the real cost of the e2e lane is the `e2e-races` job's runtime, not a mapping edit — and CLAUDE.md records that each @races observation costs ~30 s of SIM time and that this lane exists because those observations pushed the shared lane past its 720 s cap.

⚠ #9 — A CANON TENSION THE REPORT DOES NOT NAME. `SPARK_CANON.md` §7b opens with the owner's *"Once the building is built, I don't wanna see the shapes and connectors behind it. I just wanna see the building because it looks messy."* A decal adds a new non-building visible object at the tower's foot. It does NOT break the ruling — `boot-snapshot.md:38` is his later and more specific request, and the later one governs (the same pattern CLAUDE.md applies to the worktree reversal) — but the branch should say so out loud rather than let a future session read it as a regression. The report's own §G #4 (does it go under the castle / a bare lattice) is the right question and should carry this note with it.

⚠ #10 — NOTHING IN THE REPO CAN VERIFY THE ONE THING THE ROOT CAUSE ASSERTS. 'a 99 px goblin tower is composited straight onto a 0.55-alpha race backdrop with a hard silhouette edge' — whether the four S183 alpha-matted sheets already carry a baked ground shadow is a PIXEL question, answerable only by `scripts/check-atlas-scenery.mjs` (which needs `pip install numpy scipy Pillow` and is out of scope for a read-only lane). Canon §7 records that on all four sheets 'essentially ZERO pixels were fully opaque' and 19–53% sat at α 1–31, which is consistent with a soft baked shading pass. If a shadow IS baked in, a procedural decal under it double-darkens. Flag as UNVERIFIED rather than asserting a hard silhouette.

**DIRECTIONALLY RIGHT, EVIDENTIALLY SLOPPY, AND IT PRESCRIBES THE ONE CHANGE THAT BREAKS CI.**

WHAT SURVIVED. The core engineering judgement is sound and I could not dent it: procedural over atlas, published from the tower renderers rather than re-derived (`towerCover.ts:17` is the right constraint and Option B is the right answer to it), sized from `blueprintExtent` (I verified `BLUEPRINTS` is a full `Record<GodlyId, Blueprint>` at `blueprints.ts:238`, so it really does resolve for every tower), seeded off `mix32`, phased off `world.tick`, no protocol bump (PROTOCOL_VERSION 47 confirmed at `protocol.ts:704`), refusing `groundLayer` for the fog-leak reason, and calling `isConcealed` by hand because fog is per-entity culling. The `blueprintGhost` insight — the player sees the same rectangle placing and after building — is the best idea in the report and it is free. Roughly 17 of 22 evidence rows check out on the substance.

WHAT DID NOT. Three rows are wrong as evidence, and one is the S120 pattern outright: **`concealment.ts:502` does not exist — that file is 120 lines; the quote lives at `fogRenderer.ts:501`.** The root cause's grep was not run (it returns 48 lines of "sustained"-matching-"stain" noise and no `chewerRenderer.ts` hit at all), and its central assertion that "there is no ground-contact layer anywhere in the tree" is refuted by four shipped procedural ground marks, one of which — `creatureLift.ts:drawGroundMarker` — is a per-seat-coloured ground ellipse under every creature, ruled by the owner himself. Six more rows are cited 2–15 lines off. None of that changes the recommendation; all of it means the brief cannot be trusted line-for-line by a session that has not read this conversation, which is exactly what a brief is for.

THE TWO THINGS THAT WOULD HAVE COST A SESSION.
1. **The prescribed insertion point reds `e2e:gating` forever.** `e2e/fog.spec.ts` asserts `fogHiddenLayer.children` against an exact 19-entry list whose index 0 is `sparkRenderer.container`, and `e2e/tower-art.spec.ts` reads `children[6]` and `children[11]`. Five of six decals lead with a dark fill at ≤0.34 alpha and three have no bright element to carry them. The branch would pass every test it wrote and show the owner nothing.

It is one frame per state, not the animation `ART_PIPELINE.md` implies — I measured that too, because the doc is overstated and the next session should not inherit the error.
